# Plotting

Back to the [API overview](../API.md) · [README](../../README.md) · [usage guide](../USAGE.md) · [parameter reference](../PARAMETERS.md).

`amgeo_sd.plotting` — Range-time (RTI) and field-of-view figures.

| Name | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`FanPlots`](#fanplots) | A figure of ``nrows x ncols`` field-of-view maps. |
| [`apply_style`](#apply_style) | Set small, consistent matplotlib defaults (font sizes, bold titles and labels) for the figures of this package. |
| [`get_cluster_cmap`](#get_cluster_cmap) | Qualitative colour map with ``n_clusters`` shuffled colours (same shuffle as the legacy code). |
| [`RangeTimeIntervalPlot`](#rangetimeintervalplot) | A figure with stacked RTI panels for one beam. |
| [`plot_fan`](#plot_fan) | One map per entry of ``params`` for the scan nearest to ``date`` (side by side). |
| [`plot_rti`](#plot_rti) | One figure with a panel per entry of ``params`` for ``beam``. |
| [`plot_rti_compare`](#plot_rti_compare) | Stack the same beam from several tables (e.g. raw fitacf above fitacf++), identical axes and colour scale. |
| [`select_scan`](#select_scan) | Rows of the scan whose first sounding is nearest to ``date``. |

## `FanPlots`

```python
FanPlots(
    figsize = (6, 6),
    nrows: int = 1,
    ncols: int = 1,
    dpi: int = 120,
    coords: str = 'geo',
    projection: str = 'auto',
    geometry: str = 'legacy',
    altitude: float = 300.0,
)
```

A figure of ``nrows x ncols`` field-of-view maps.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `figsize` | (float, float) | `(6, 6)` | Figure size in inches. |
| `nrows`, `ncols` | int | `1` | Panel layout; one map is added per `plot_fov` / `plot_layfovs` call, row by row. |
| `dpi` | int | `120` | Resolution of the figure on screen. |
| `coords` | ``"geo"`` or ``"aacgmv2"`` | `'geo'` | Coordinate frame of the map. |
| `projection` | ``"auto"``, ``"polar"`` or ``"ortho"`` | `'auto'` | ``auto`` is orthographic around the field of view, or polar stereographic above 70 deg latitude. |
| `geometry` | ``"legacy"`` or ``"pydarn"`` | `'legacy'` | Field-of-view implementation, see [`radar_fov`](geo.md#radar_fov). |
| `altitude` | float | `300.0` | Height of the range cells [km], also used for the conversion to AACGM. |

**Examples**

```python
fan = FanPlots(nrows=1, ncols=2, figsize=(11, 5.5))
fan.plot_fov(frame, datetime(2025, 2, 8, 3, 0), "bks", param="v")
fan.plot_fov(frame, datetime(2025, 2, 8, 3, 0), "bks", param="gflg_kde")
fan.save("fan.png")
```

### `FanPlots.overlay_radar`

```python
overlay_radar(ax, rad: str, date: dt.datetime, color: str = 'darkblue')
```

Mark the radar site and label it with the radar code.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ax` | cartopy GeoAxes | required | Map returned by `plot_fov`. |
| `rad` | str | required | Radar code; its site is read from the hardware file valid on ``date``. |
| `date` | datetime | required | UTC date (hardware epoch, and AACGM epoch for ``coords="aacgmv2"``). |
| `color` | str | `'darkblue'` | Marker and label colour. |

### `FanPlots.overlay_fov`

```python
overlay_fov(ax, fov_lat: np.ndarray, fov_lon: np.ndarray, color: str = 'k', lw: float = 1.0)
```

Outline of the field of view (all beams, gates 0..ngates).

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ax` | cartopy GeoAxes | required | Map to draw on. |
| `fov_lat`, `fov_lon` | ndarray | required | Cell corners of shape ``(nbeams + 1, ngates + 1)`` in the map's frame (``glat``/``glon`` of [`radar_fov`](geo.md#radar_fov), converted when ``coords="aacgmv2"``). |
| `color` | str | `'k'` | Line colour. |
| `lw` | float | `1.0` | Line width. |

### `FanPlots.plot_fov`

```python
plot_fov(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    date: dt.datetime,
    rad: str,
    param: str = 'v',
    gflg_mask: str | None = 'gflg',
    add_colorbar: bool = True,
    title: str = '',
    vrange: tuple[float, float, float] | None = None,
    max_gate: int | None = None,
    terminator: bool = False,
)
```

Draw the scan nearest to ``date``: echoes coloured by ``param``; ground scatter (``gflg_mask`` == 1) gray.

``param`` may also be a flag column (``gflg``, ``gflg_conv``, ``gflg_kde``, ``gflg_ribiero``), drawn with the
IS / GS / undetermined classes.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `df` | pandas.DataFrame | required | Echo table with ``time``, ``scnum``, ``bmnum``, ``slist``, ``nrang``, ``frang``, ``rsep``, ``param`` and, for the mask, ``gflg_mask``. |
| `date` | datetime | required | Time of the scan to draw; the scan starting nearest to it is used (UTC, naive). |
| `rad` | str | required | Radar code, selects the geometry. |
| `param` | str | `'v'` | Column to colour by: ``v``, ``w_l``, ``p_l``, ``v_mad``, another numeric column, or a flag column. |
| `gflg_mask` | str or None | `'gflg'` | Flag column whose value 1 marks ground scatter, drawn gray under a ``GS`` legend (numeric ``param`` only); ``None`` draws everything in colour. |
| `add_colorbar` | bool | `True` | Draw a colour bar (numeric ``param`` only). |
| `title` | str | `''` | Text at the top left; the radar code when empty. |
| `vrange` | (float, float, float), optional | `None` | ``(vmin, vmax, step)`` of the colour scale. Defaults: velocity -30..30 m/s in 5 m/s steps, width 0..100, power 0..30, v_mad 0..30. |
| `max_gate` | int, optional | `None` | Draw only gates below this number; all gates when ``None``. |
| `terminator` | bool | `False` | Shade the night side (geographic coordinates only). |

**Returns**

- *cartopy GeoAxes* — The map.

## `apply_style`

```python
apply_style() -> None
```

Set small, consistent matplotlib defaults (font sizes, bold titles and labels) for the figures of this package.

The plotting functions call it themselves; call it yourself only to get the same look in your own figures.

## `get_cluster_cmap`

```python
get_cluster_cmap(n_clusters: int, plot_noise: bool = False) -> mcolors.ListedColormap
```

Qualitative colour map with ``n_clusters`` shuffled colours (same shuffle as the legacy code).

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n_clusters` | int | required | Number of colours (cluster labels) the map must cover; it repeats the base colours when more are needed. |
| `plot_noise` | bool | `False` | Make the first entry black so that label -1 (noise) is drawn black. |

**Returns**

- *matplotlib.colors.ListedColormap* — The colour map, named ``"cluster"``.

## `RangeTimeIntervalPlot`

```python
RangeTimeIntervalPlot(
    nrang: int = 75,
    xlim = None,
    fig_title: str = '',
    num_subplots: int = 3,
    figsize = None,
    dpi: int = 100,
)
```

A figure with stacked RTI panels for one beam.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `nrang` | int | `75` | Number of range gates shown (y axis 0..nrang). |
| `xlim` | (datetime, datetime), optional | `None` | Time axis limits (UT). Defaults to the span of the first table added. |
| `fig_title` | str | `''` | Figure title, drawn at the top left. |
| `num_subplots` | int | `3` | Number of panels; add them with the ``add_*`` methods. |
| `figsize` | (float, float), optional | `None` | Figure size in inches; default width 9, height 2.6 per panel. |
| `dpi` | int | `100` | Resolution of the figure on screen. |

**Examples**

```python
rti = RangeTimeIntervalPlot(nrang=75, num_subplots=2)
rti.add_param(frame, beam=12, title="(a) velocity", param="v")
rti.add_gsis(frame, beam=12, title="(b) flag", flag="gflg_kde", xlabel="Time [UT]")
rti.save("rti.png")
```

### `RangeTimeIntervalPlot.add_param`

```python
add_param(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    beam: int,
    title: str = '',
    param: str = 'v',
    vmin = None,
    vmax = None,
    step = None,
    cmap: str | None = None,
    label: str | None = None,
    xlabel: str = '',
    ylabel: str = 'Range gate',
)
```

Colour-coded ``param`` (``v``, ``w_l``, ``p_l``, ``v_mad`` or any numeric column) versus time and gate.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `df` | pandas.DataFrame | required | Echo table ([`load_frame`](io.md#load_frame)) with ``time``, ``bmnum``, ``slist`` and ``param``. |
| `beam` | int | required | Beam number to draw; ``ValueError`` when it has no echoes. |
| `title` | str | `''` | Panel title (drawn at the left). |
| `param` | str | `'v'` | Column to colour by. ``v``, ``w_l``, ``p_l`` and ``v_mad`` have preset ranges and colour maps; any other numeric column needs ``vmin`` and ``vmax``. |
| `vmin`, `vmax` | float, optional | `None` | Colour range. Defaults: velocity -100..100 m/s, width 0..200 m/s, power 0..30 dB, v_mad 0..60 m/s. |
| `step` | float, optional | `None` | Width of a colour bin; default per parameter, or (``vmax`` - ``vmin``) / 8 for other columns. |
| `cmap` | str, optional | `None` | Matplotlib colour map name; default per parameter (``jet_r``, ``viridis``, ``plasma``, ``magma``). |
| `label` | str, optional | `None` | Colour-bar label; default the parameter's name and unit. |
| `xlabel` | str | `''` | x-axis label. |
| `ylabel` | str | `'Range gate'` | y-axis label. |

**Returns**

- *matplotlib.axes.Axes* — The new panel.

### `RangeTimeIntervalPlot.add_gsis`

```python
add_gsis(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    beam: int,
    title: str = '',
    flag: str = 'gflg',
    xlabel: str = '',
    ylabel: str = 'Range gate',
)
```

Ionospheric / ground scatter classification from the flag column ``flag``.

IS (ionospheric) is red, GS (ground) blue, US (unclassified, -1) black and undetermined (2) green.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `df` | pandas.DataFrame | required | Echo table with ``time``, ``bmnum``, ``slist`` and the flag column. |
| `beam` | int | required | Beam number to draw. |
| `title` | str | `''` | Panel title. |
| `flag` | str | `'gflg'` | Flag column: ``gflg`` (fit / legacy median rule), ``gflg_conv``, ``gflg_kde`` (median model) or ``gflg_ribiero`` (DBSCAN model). |
| `xlabel` | str | `''` | x-axis label. |
| `ylabel` | str | `'Range gate'` | y-axis label. |

**Returns**

- *matplotlib.axes.Axes* — The new panel.

### `RangeTimeIntervalPlot.add_clusters`

```python
add_clusters(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    beam: int,
    title: str = '',
    column: str = 'cluster_tag',
    label_clusters: bool = True,
    xlabel: str = '',
    ylabel: str = 'Range gate',
)
```

Cluster membership (``column``: ``cluster_tag`` from the clustering models); noise (-1) is black.

``clabel`` of the median model is a *per-scan* DBSCAN label, not continuous in time, so it is rarely
meaningful here.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `df` | pandas.DataFrame | required | Echo table with ``time``, ``bmnum``, ``slist`` and the label column. |
| `beam` | int | required | Beam number to draw. |
| `title` | str | `''` | Panel title. |
| `column` | str | `'cluster_tag'` | Label column; ``ValueError`` when absent (cluster plots need the output of the DBSCAN model). |
| `label_clusters` | bool | `True` | Write the cluster number on large clusters (more than 250 echoes, or any cluster when there are fewer than 50). |
| `xlabel` | str | `''` | x-axis label. |
| `ylabel` | str | `'Range gate'` | y-axis label. |

**Returns**

- *matplotlib.axes.Axes* — The new panel.

## `plot_fan`

```python
plot_fan(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    rad: str,
    date: dt.datetime,
    params: Sequence[str] = ('v',),
    path: str | os.PathLike | None = None,
    coords: str = 'geo',
    projection: str = 'auto',
    kind: str = '',
    gflg_mask: str | None = 'gflg',
    dpi: int = 120,
    geometry: str = 'legacy',
    altitude: float = 300.0,
    **kwargs,
) -> FanPlots
```

One map per entry of ``params`` for the scan nearest to ``date`` (side by side).

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `df` | pandas.DataFrame | required | Echo table from [`load_frame`](io.md#load_frame) (raw fitacf or fitacf++). |
| `rad` | str | required | Radar code, selects the geometry. |
| `date` | datetime | required | Time of the scan to draw (UTC, naive); the scan starting nearest to it is used. |
| `params` | sequence of str | `('v',)` | One map per entry: numeric columns (``v``, ``w_l``, ``p_l``, ``v_mad``) or flag columns (``gflg``, ``gflg_conv``, ``gflg_kde``, ``gflg_ribiero``). |
| `path` | str or path, optional | `None` | Save the figure here; not saved when ``None``. |
| `coords` | ``"geo"`` or ``"aacgmv2"`` | `'geo'` | Coordinate frame of the maps. |
| `projection` | ``"auto"``, ``"polar"`` or ``"ortho"`` | `'auto'` | Map projection, see [`FanPlots`](plotting.md#fanplots). |
| `kind` | str | `''` | Description of the data (``"fitacf++"``, ...) added to the panel title. |
| `gflg_mask` | str or None | `'gflg'` | Flag column whose value 1 is drawn gray in numeric maps; ``None`` for no mask. |
| `dpi` | int | `120` | Resolution. |
| `geometry` | ``"legacy"`` or ``"pydarn"`` | `'legacy'` | Field-of-view implementation, see [`radar_fov`](geo.md#radar_fov). |
| `altitude` | float | `300.0` | Height of the range cells [km]. |
| `**kwargs` | keyword arguments |  | Passed to [`FanPlots.plot_fov`](plotting.md#fanplotsplot_fov): ``add_colorbar``, ``vrange``, ``max_gate``, ``terminator``. |

**Returns**

- *FanPlots* — The figure object (``.fig`` is the matplotlib figure); call ``.close()`` when done.

## `plot_rti`

```python
plot_rti(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    beam: int,
    params: Sequence[str] = ('v', 'w_l', 'p_l', 'gflg'),
    path: str | os.PathLike | None = None,
    rad: str = '',
    nrang: int | None = None,
    xlim = None,
    kind: str = '',
    dpi: int = 120,
) -> RangeTimeIntervalPlot
```

One figure with a panel per entry of ``params`` for ``beam``.

Entries are numeric columns (``v``, ``w_l``, ``p_l``, ``v_mad``), flag columns (``gflg``, ``gflg_conv``,
``gflg_kde``, ``gflg_ribiero``) or ``cluster_tag``.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `df` | pandas.DataFrame | required | Echo table from [`load_frame`](io.md#load_frame) (raw fitacf or fitacf++, same columns). |
| `beam` | int | required | Beam number to draw. |
| `params` | sequence of str | `('v', 'w_l', 'p_l', 'gflg')` | One panel per entry, top to bottom. |
| `path` | str or path, optional | `None` | Save the figure here (the format follows the extension); not saved when ``None``. |
| `rad` | str | `''` | Radar code for the title. |
| `nrang` | int, optional | `None` | Number of range gates on the y axis; the largest ``nrang`` of the data when ``None``. |
| `xlim` | (datetime, datetime), optional | `None` | Time limits; the span of the data when ``None``. |
| `kind` | str | `''` | Description of the data (e.g. ``"fitacf 2.5"``, ``"fitacf++"``) appended to the title. |
| `dpi` | int | `120` | Resolution. |

**Returns**

- *RangeTimeIntervalPlot* — The figure object (``.fig`` is the matplotlib figure); call ``.close()`` when done.

## `plot_rti_compare`

```python
plot_rti_compare(
    frames: Mapping[str, pd.DataFrame],
    beam: int,
    param: str = 'v',
    path: str | os.PathLike | None = None,
    rad: str = '',
    nrang: int | None = None,
    flag: str | None = None,
    dpi: int = 120,
) -> RangeTimeIntervalPlot
```

Stack the same beam from several tables (e.g. raw fitacf above fitacf++), identical axes and colour scale.

With ``flag`` (a flag column such as ``gflg``) each dataset also gets a classification panel.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frames` | mapping of str to pandas.DataFrame | required | Panel label (e.g. ``"raw fitacf"``) to echo table; drawn in this order. |
| `beam` | int | required | Beam number to draw. |
| `param` | str | `'v'` | Numeric column drawn for every dataset, with one shared colour scale. |
| `path` | str or path, optional | `None` | Save the figure here; not saved when ``None``. |
| `rad` | str | `''` | Radar code for the title. |
| `nrang` | int, optional | `None` | Number of range gates on the y axis; the largest ``nrang`` of the tables when ``None``. |
| `flag` | str, optional | `None` | Flag column; adds a classification panel under each dataset. |
| `dpi` | int | `120` | Resolution. |

**Returns**

- *RangeTimeIntervalPlot* — The figure object; call ``.close()`` when done.

## `select_scan`

```python
select_scan(df: pd.DataFrame, date: dt.datetime) -> pd.DataFrame
```

Rows of the scan whose first sounding is nearest to ``date``.

**Parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `df` | pandas.DataFrame | required | Echo table with ``time`` and ``scnum`` (from [`load_frame`](io.md#load_frame) or [`scans_to_dataframe`](io.md#scans_to_dataframe)). |
| `date` | datetime | required | Requested time (UTC, naive). |

**Returns**

- *pandas.DataFrame* — The rows of the scan whose earliest echo time is closest to ``date``.

**Raises**

- *ValueError* — When the table is empty or has no ``scnum`` column.
